m.d:
This property determines whether right-to-left (RTL) text layout is applied to the text of GuiObjects in the experience, which is needed to correctly display languages written right-to-left, such as Arabic and Hebrew.

The default value is RtlTextSupport.Default. Both RtlTextSupport.Default and RtlTextSupport.Enabled turn RTL text layout support on, while RtlTextSupport.Disabled turns it off.
m.s: Controls whether right-to-left (RTL) text layout is enabled for text in `Class.GuiObject|GuiObjects` throughout the experience.

kid.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). Turns on right-to-left text layout for languages like Arabic and Hebrew. On by default.

m.d:
This property sets the preferred screen orientation mode for users with mobile devices. For the different modes available, see ScreenOrientation.

By default, this property is set to Sensor, meaning the experience is displayed depending on the best match to the device's current orientation, either landscape (left/right) or portrait.

When a Player joins the experience on a mobile device, this property determines the device's starting orientation and sets that player's PlayerGui.ScreenOrientation accordingly. You can also get the player's current screen orientation through PlayerGui.CurrentScreenOrientation, useful when using one of the "sensor" ScreenOrientation settings.

Note that changing this property will not change the screen orientation for Players already in the experience. To change the orientation for an existing player, use their PlayerGui.ScreenOrientation property.
m.s: Sets the default screen orientation mode for users with mobile devices.

kid.simple: The screen direction phones and tablets start in: landscape (sideways), portrait (upright), or Sensor (follows how they hold the device, the default). Changing it later doesn't affect players already in the game; change their PlayerGui.ScreenOrientation for that.
kid.example: game:GetService("StarterGui").ScreenOrientation = Enum.ScreenOrientation.LandscapeSensor

m.d: This property determines whether the contents of StarterGui is visible in Studio.
m.s: Determines whether the contents of `Class.StarterGui` is visible in Studio.

kid.simple: Whether StarterGui's UI is shown in the Studio editor while you build. Doesn't affect the running game.

m.d:
This property determines whether the gamepad virtual cursor, which lets players move a pointer across on-screen GuiObjects using a controller, is enabled.

The default value is VirtualCursorMode.Default. Setting it to VirtualCursorMode.Enabled turns the virtual cursor on and VirtualCursorMode.Disabled turns it off. When a player is in VR, the virtual cursor is always active regardless of this property's value.
m.s: Controls whether the gamepad virtual cursor is enabled for navigating `Class.GuiObject|GuiObjects` with a controller.

kid.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). Turns the gamepad virtual cursor on or off, which lets controller players move a pointer over buttons. Always on in VR.

m.d:
This method returns data set or made available by Roblox's core scripts. The first and only parameter is a string that selects the information to be fetched. The following sections describe the strings and the data they return by this function.

Calling this method may yield. Many of these also register an equivalent SetCore() function (these are marked with an asterisk).

PointsNotificationsActive *

Returns true if player point notifications are enabled.

BadgesNotificationsActive *

Returns true if badge notifications are enabled.

AvatarContextMenuEnabled *

Returns true if the Avatar Context Menu is enabled.

ChatActive *

Returns whether the chat is active or not. This is indicated by the selection state of the top bar's chat icon.

ChatWindowSize *

Returns the size of the chat window as a UDim2.

ChatWindowPosition *

Returns the size of the chat window as a UDim2.

ChatBarDisabled *

Returns true if the chat bar is disabled.

GetBlockedUserIds

Returns a list of UserIds associated with users that have been blocked by the local player.

PlayerBlockedEvent

Returns a BindableEvent that is fired whenever a player is blocked by the local player.

PlayerUnblockedEvent

Returns a BindableEvent that is fired whenever a player is unblocked by the local player.

PlayerMutedEvent

Returns a BindableEvent that is fired whenever a player is muted by the local player.

PlayerUnmutedEvent

Returns a BindableEvent that is fired whenever a player is unmuted by the local player.

PlayerFriendedEvent

Returns a BindableEvent that is fired whenever a player is connected by the local player.

PlayerUnfriendedEvent

Returns a BindableEvent that is fired whenever a player is unconnected by the local player.

DevConsoleVisible *

Returns true if the Developer Console is visible.

VRRotationIntensity

Returns a string describing the camera rotation sensitivity in VR: Low, High and Smooth. This will not be available unless VRService.VREnabled is true.
m.s: Returns a variable that has been specified by a Roblox core script.

p.s: The name of the core parameter to retrieve, such as "PointsNotificationsActive" or "ChatActive".

r.s: The value associated with the specified core parameter name, whose type depends on the parameter queried.

kid.simple: Reads a setting or info from Roblox's built-in UI, picked by name, like "PointsNotificationsActive" or "GetBlockedUserIds". Use it in a LocalScript. It may pause briefly.
kid.example:
-- LocalScript
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
local blocked = StarterGui:GetCore("GetBlockedUserIds")
print("You have blocked " .. #blocked .. " users")

m.d:
This function returns whether the given CoreGuiTypeis enabled, or if it has been disabled using StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(). This function should be called on the client.

Note that setting "TopbarEnabled" to false using SetCore() hides all CoreGuiTypes but does not affect the result of this function.
m.s: Returns whether the given `Enum.CoreGuiType`is enabled, or if it has been disabled using `Class.StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled()`.

p.s: The given CoreGuiType.

r.s: Whether the given CoreGuiType is enabled.

kid.simple: Tells you if a built-in UI piece (like the Backpack or PlayerList) is turned on. Call it in a LocalScript.
kid.example:
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
print(StarterGui:GetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack))

m.d:
This method (not to be confused with SetCoreGuiEnabled()) exposes a variety of functionality defined by Roblox's core scripts, such as sending notifications, toggling notifications for badges/points, defining a callback for the reset button, or toggling the topbar.

The first parameter is a string that selects the functionality with which the call will interact. It may be necessary to call this method multiple times using LuaGlobals.pcall() in case the respective core script has not yet loaded (or if it has been disabled entirely).

The following table describes the strings that may be accepted as the first parameter. The parameters that should follow are dependent on the functionality that will be used and are described in sub-tables.

ChatActive

Controls whether the chat is active.

Name Type Default Description
active boolean (required) Determines whether the chat should be made active.
PointsNotificationsActive

Controls whether notifications for earned player points will appear.

Name Type Default Description
active boolean (required) Determines whether notifications for earned player points will appear.
BadgesNotificationsActive

Controls whether notifications for earned badges will appear.

Name Type Default Description
active boolean (required) Determines whether notifications for earned badges will appear.
ResetButtonCallback

Determines the behavior, if any, of the reset button given a boolean or a BindableEvent to be fired when a player requests to reset.

Name Type Default Description
enabled boolean (required) Determines whether the reset button retains its default behavior.
OR
callback Class.BindableEvent (required) A Class.BindableEvent to be fired when the player confirms they want to reset.
ChatMakeSystemMessage

Display a formatted message in the chat. Using this method requires the experience's TextChatService.ChatVersion to be set to LegacyChatService, although legacy chat is deprecated and usage is discouraged. For experiences using the current TextChatService, refer to TextChannel:DisplaySystemMessage().

Name Type Default Description
configTable dictionary (required) A dictionary of information describing the message (see below).
Name Type Default Description
Text string (required) The message to display.
Color Datatype.Color3 Datatype.Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 243) Text color of the message.
Font Enum.Font SourceSansBold Font of the message.
TextSize integer 18 Text size of the message.
SendNotification

Causes a non-intrusive notification to appear at the bottom right of the screen. The notification may have up to two buttons.

Name Type Default Description
configTable dictionary (required) A dictionary of information describing the notification (see below).
Name Type Default Description
Title string (required) The title of the notification.
Text string (required) The main text of the notification.
Icon string The image to display with the notification.
Duration number 5 Duration (in seconds) the notification should stay visible.
Callback Class.BindableFunction A Class.BindableFunction that should be invoked with the text of the button pressed by the player.
Button1 string The text to display on the first button.
Button2 string The text to display on the second button.
TopbarEnabled

Determines whether the topbar is displayed. Disabling the topbar will also disable all CoreGuis such as the chat, inventory, and player list (for example, those set with SetCoreGuiEnabled).

When disabled, the region the topbar once occupied will still capture mouse events; however, buttons placed there will not respond to clicks. The origin of GUI space will still be offset 36 pixels from the top of the screen.

Name Type Default Description
enabled boolean (required) Determines whether the topbar should be visible.
DevConsoleVisible

Determines whether the Developer Console is visible.

Name Type Default Description
visibility boolean (required) Determines whether the console is visible.
PromptSendFriendRequest

Prompts the current player to send a friend request to the given Player.

Name Type Default Description
player Class.Player (required) The player to which the friend request should be sent.
PromptUnfriend

Prompts the current player to remove a given Player from their friends list.

Name Type Default Description
player Class.Player (required) The player who should be unconnected.
PromptBlockPlayer

Prompts the current player to block the given Player.

Name Type Default Description
player Class.Player (required) The player who should be blocked.
PromptUnblockPlayer

Prompts the current player to unblock the given Player.

Name Type Default Description
player Class.Player (required) The player who should be unblocked.
AvatarContextMenuEnabled

Determines whether the Avatar Context Menu is enabled.

Name Type Default Description
enabled boolean (required) Determines whether the context menu is enabled.
AvatarContextMenuTarget

Forcibly opens the Avatar Context Menu.

Name Type Default Description
player Class.Player (required) The player on whom the context menu will be opened.
AddAvatarContextMenuOption

Adds an option to the Avatar Context Menu.

Name Type Default Description
option Enum.AvatarContextMenuOption (required) Option to add.
OR
option table (required) A two-element table, where the first is the name of the custom action, and the second is a Class.BindableEvent which will be fired with a player was selected when the option was activated.
RemoveAvatarContextMenuOption

Removes an option to the Avatar Context Menu. The option argument must be the same as what was used with "AddAvatarContextMenuOption" (see above).

Name Type Default Description
option Variant (required) The same value provided to AddAvatarContextMenuOption.
AvatarContextMenuTheme

Configures the customizable Avatar Context Menu which is an opt-in feature that allows easy player-to-player social interaction via custom actions, such as initiating trades, battles, and more. For more info on how to customize its theme, see the Avatar Context Menu article.

CoreGuiChatConnections

Sets up a bindable gateway connection between the CoreGui topbar's chat button and the legacy chat system. The second parameter must be a table of BindableEvents and BindableFunctions.
m.s: Allows you to perform certain interactions with Roblox's core scripts.

p.s: Selects the functionality with which the call will interact.
A table of BindableEvents and BindableFunctions.

kid.simple: Changes or uses a feature of Roblox's built-in UI, picked by name. Popular ones: "SendNotification" (pop-up message), "ResetButtonCallback" (false turns off the reset button), "TopbarEnabled", "PromptSendFriendRequest". Use in a LocalScript, wrapped in pcall.
kid.example:
-- LocalScript: turn off the Reset Character button
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
pcall(function()
    StarterGui:SetCore("ResetButtonCallback", false)
end)
kid.gotcha: It errors if Roblox's UI scripts haven't loaded yet. Retry with pcall and task.wait.

m.d:
This function sets whether the CoreGui element associated with the given CoreGuiType is enabled or disabled.

The top bar cannot be disabled using this function. To disable it, set "TopbarEnabled" to false using StarterGui:SetCore().
m.s: Sets whether the `Class.CoreGui` element associated with the given `Enum.CoreGuiType` is enabled or disabled.

p.s: The given CoreGuiType.
Whether to enable or disable the given CoreGuiType.

kid.simple: Turns a built-in UI piece on or off for this player: chat, player list, backpack hotbar, health, emotes menu, or All. Call it in a LocalScript.
kid.example:
-- LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts: make your own inventory instead
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, false)
kid.gotcha: It can't hide the top bar. Use SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false) for that.

kid.simple: StarterGui is where you build your game's on-screen UI (buttons, health bars, menus) in Studio. When a player's character spawns, everything in StarterGui is copied into that player's own PlayerGui, which is what they actually see. It also has methods to hide or change Roblox's built-in UI, like the chat, the player list, and the backpack bar.
kid.analogy: StarterGui is like the master copy of a worksheet on the teacher's desk. Each student (player) gets their own photocopy (PlayerGui) to write on. Writing on the master copy during class doesn't change the copies students already have.
whenToUse: Design ScreenGuis (buttons, text, menus) in Studio that every player should get.
Hide Roblox's built-in UI, like the player list or the backpack hotbar (SetCoreGuiEnabled).
Show a little notification in the corner (SetCore "SendNotification").
Turn off the reset button (SetCore "ResetButtonCallback").
kid.where: A service in the Explorer. Get it with `game:GetService("StarterGui")`. Put ScreenGuis inside it in Studio. Call SetCore, GetCore, SetCoreGuiEnabled and GetCoreGuiEnabled from a LocalScript, because they change one player's screen.

terms.UI / GUI: User interface: the buttons, text, pictures and menus drawn on the screen.
terms.ScreenGui: A container for 2D UI that draws on the player's screen. Put buttons and labels inside it.
terms.PlayerGui: A folder inside each Player that holds the UI that player actually sees. Filled with copies from StarterGui.
terms.CoreGui: Roblox's own built-in UI: chat, player list, backpack hotbar, health bar, emotes menu, and the top bar.
terms.ResetOnSpawn: A property on ScreenGui. If true (default), that ScreenGui is deleted and re-copied every time the character respawns. If false, it's copied once and stays.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI scripts are LocalScripts.
terms.Enum.CoreGuiType: The list of built-in UI pieces you can turn on or off, like PlayerList, Backpack, Chat, Health, EmotesMenu, or All.
terms.pcall: Runs a function safely: if it errors, your script keeps going. Useful for SetCore, which can fail if Roblox's UI hasn't loaded yet.
terms.yield: Pause and wait. GetCore can pause your script for a moment.

examples.title: How StarterGui gets to the player's screen
examples.place: LocalScript inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer

-- This script was COPIED from StarterGui into the player's PlayerGui.
-- script.Parent is the copy of the ScreenGui the player sees.
local screenGui = script.Parent
print(screenGui:GetFullName()) -- e.g. Players.YourName.PlayerGui.ScreenGui

-- If screenGui.ResetOnSpawn is true (the default), this whole ScreenGui
-- (and this script) is deleted and copied fresh every respawn.
-- Set it to false to keep things like scores on screen across deaths.
screenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false
explain: In Studio you build the UI inside StarterGui. That's the template.
When a character spawns, Roblox copies StarterGui's children into that player's PlayerGui. The copy is what shows on screen.
Because of the copy, script.Parent is the player's own ScreenGui, not the one in StarterGui.
ScreenGuis with ResetOnSpawn = true are replaced every respawn. With false, they are copied once and stay.
To change what one player sees during the game, change their PlayerGui, not StarterGui.

examples.title: Hide the player list and show a notification
examples.code:
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")

-- Hide the built-in player list in the top-right corner
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.PlayerList, false)

-- SetCore can fail if Roblox's UI isn't ready yet, so try a few times
local success = false
for attempt = 1, 5 do
    success = pcall(function()
        StarterGui:SetCore("SendNotification", {
            Title = "Welcome!",
            Text = "Reach the top to win.",
            Duration = 5, -- seconds
        })
    end)
    if success then
        break
    end
    task.wait(1)
end
explain: SetCoreGuiEnabled turns a built-in UI piece on or off for this player.
SetCore("SendNotification", {...}) pops up a small message at the bottom right.
We use pcall and retry because SetCore errors if Roblox's own UI scripts haven't loaded yet.

gotchas: Changing StarterGui while the game runs doesn't change what players already see. Edit player.PlayerGui instead (or wait for them to respawn).
SetCore, GetCore and SetCoreGuiEnabled must be called from a LocalScript.
SetCore can error if called too early. Wrap it in pcall and retry.
If Players.CharacterAutoLoads is false, StarterGui isn't copied until the character is loaded with LoadCharacterAsync.
The top bar can't be hidden with SetCoreGuiEnabled. Use SetCore("TopbarEnabled", false).

class/StarterPack.d:
StarterPack is a service-level container whose contents are copied into each player's Backpack when their player character spawns. It is generally used to hold Tools but it can also hold LocalScripts to ensure that each player gets a copy.

To ensure that certain Tools are available to specific players instead of all players (StarterPack), use player‑specific StarterGear containers or parent those Tools directly to player Backpacks.
class/StarterPack.s: A container whose contents are copied into each player's `Class.Backpack` when their player character spawns. It is generally used to hold `Class.Tool|Tools`.

class/StarterPlayer.d:
A service which allows the defaults of properties in the Player object to be set. When a player enters the server, each property of the player object is set to the current value of the corresponding property in StarterPlayer.

Additionally, you may add four objects to this service:

  • A StarterPlayerScripts instance with scripts that run once for each player.
  • A StarterCharacterScripts instance with scripts to add to each player's character every time they spawn.
  • A Humanoid instance named StarterHumanoid which will be used as the default humanoid for each player's character.
  • A Model instance named StarterCharacter which will be used as the character model for all players.
class/StarterPlayer.s: A service which allows the defaults of properties in the `Class.Player` object to be set.

m.d:
This property describes the current game's permission levels regarding custom avatar Animations from the website.

As such, this value cannot be changed from within the game. It can only be changed by changing the game's permission levels within the game's setting's page on the website.

This property is not intended for use in the game.
m.s: Describes the current game's permission levels regarding custom avatar animations from the website.

kid.simple: Hidden. Shows whether your game allows players' own avatar animations. Set on the game's settings page, not by scripts.

m.d:
This property sets whether the character will automatically jump when hitting an obstacle on a mobile device.

This property is copied from the StarterPlayer to a Player when they join the game. Following that. the value of this property is copied to Humanoid.AutoJumpEnabled property of the character's Humanoid on spawn. In other words, it is possible to set the auto-jump behavior on a per-character, per-player and per-game basis using these three properties.
m.s: Sets whether the character will automatically jump when hitting an obstacle on a mobile device.

kid.simple: Starting value for auto-jump on phones and tablets: the character hops over small obstacles by itself. Copied to Player.AutoJumpEnabled, then to the Humanoid.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.AutoJumpEnabled = false

m.d: This property controls the rollout state of new AnimationConstraint joints in avatars. When disabled, avatars spawn with legacy Motor6Ds connecting their limbs. When enabled, avatars spawn with AnimationConstraints and BallSocketConstraints connecting their limbs. This makes it easier to write scripts that enable physical simulation, like arm strength and ragdoll falling down.
m.s: Controls whether avatars spawn with `Class.AnimationConstraint` joints for physical simulation.

kid.simple: Internal Roblox setting (scripts can't use it). Controls whether avatars use newer physics joints that make ragdolls easier.

m.d:
This property sets the maximum distance in studs the camera can be from the character with the default cameras.

This property sets the default value of Player.CameraMaxZoomDistance for each player who joins the game. If this value is set to a lower value than StarterPlayer.CameraMinZoomDistance it will be increased to CameraMinZoomDistance.
m.s: The maximum distance the player's default camera is allowed to zoom out in studs.

kid.simple: Starting value for how far (in studs) players can zoom the camera out. Copied to Player.CameraMaxZoomDistance when they join.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CameraMaxZoomDistance = 50

m.d:
This property sets the minimum distance in studs the camera can be from the character with the default cameras.

This property sets the default value of Player.CameraMinZoomDistance for each player who joins the game. If this value is set to a higher value than StarterPlayer.CameraMaxZoomDistance it will be decreased to CameraMaxZoomDistance.
m.s: The minimum distance in studs the player's default camera is allowed to zoom in.

kid.simple: Starting value for how close (in studs) players can zoom in. Copied to Player.CameraMinZoomDistance when they join.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CameraMinZoomDistance = 2

m.d:
Sets the default value for Player.CameraMode for each player in the game. The camera has two modes:

First Person

In first person mode, the player's camera is zoomed all the way in. Unless there is a visible GUI present with the GuiButton.Modal property set to true, the mouse will be locked and the user's camera will turn as the mouse moves.

Third Person

In third person mode (default), the character can be seen in the camera. While in third person mode on Roblox:

  • You may right-click and drag to rotate your camera, or use the arrow keys at the bottom right-hand corner of the screen.
  • When you move your mouse, your camera does not change (unless you move the mouse to the end of the screen).
  • When you press any of the arrow keys, the user's character will face in the corresponding arrow key's direction.
  • You can zoom in and out freely.
m.s: Changes the default camera's mode to either first or third person.

kid.simple: Starting camera mode for players: Classic (third person, the default) or LockFirstPerson (first person).
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CameraMode = Enum.CameraMode.LockFirstPerson

m.d:
This property determines the starting value of Humanoid.BreakJointsOnDeath for a player's Player.Character.

Note that AvatarJointUpgrade must be enabled for this property to take effect.
m.s: Determines the starting value of `Class.Humanoid.BreakJointsOnDeath` for `Class.Player.Character`.

kid.simple: Starting value for Humanoid.BreakJointsOnDeath on player characters (whether the body falls apart on death). Only works when the AvatarJointUpgrade setting is on.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CharacterBreakJointsOnDeath = false

m.d:
This property determines the starting value of Humanoid.JumpHeight for a player's Player.Character in studs, with a default of 7.2.

This property is only visible in the Properties window If CharacterUseJumpPower is set to false, as it would not be relevant otherwise.

Since this property is only relevant for characters being spawned in the future, changing it will not change any existing player characters. Changes to this property will only take effect when a player respawns.
m.s: Determines the starting value of `Class.Humanoid.JumpHeight` for `Class.Player.Character`.

kid.simple: Starting jump height in studs (default 7.2). Used when CharacterUseJumpPower is false. Takes effect when characters respawn.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CharacterJumpHeight = 12

m.d:
This property determines the starting value of Humanoid.JumpPower for a player's Player.Character, with a default of 50, minimum of 0, and maximum of 1000.

This property is only visible in the Properties window If CharacterUseJumpPower is set to true, as it would not be relevant otherwise.

Since this property is only relevant for characters being spawned in the future, changing it will not change any existing player characters. Changes to this property will only take effect when a player respawns.
m.s: Determines the starting value of `Class.Humanoid.JumpPower` for `Class.Player.Character`.

kid.simple: Starting jump strength (default 50, from 0 to 1000). Used when CharacterUseJumpPower is true. Takes effect when characters respawn.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CharacterJumpPower = 80

m.d:
This property determines the starting value of Humanoid.MaxSlopeAngle for a player's Player.Character in degrees. It defaults to 89, so humanoids can climb pretty much any slope they want by default.

Since this property is only relevant for characters being spawned in the future, changing it will not change any existing player characters. Changes to this property will only take effect when a player respawns.
m.s: Determines the starting value of `Class.Humanoid.MaxSlopeAngle` for `Class.Player.Character`.

kid.simple: Starting steepest slope (in degrees) characters can walk up. Default 89. Takes effect on respawn.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CharacterMaxSlopeAngle = 45

m.d:
This property determines the starting value of Humanoid.UseJumpPower for a player's Player.Character. Toggling it will change which property is visible in the Properties window (CharacterJumpHeight if false or CharacterJumpPower if true). Defaults to true.

Since this property is only relevant for characters being spawned in the future, changing it will not change any existing player characters. Changes to this property will only take effect when a player respawns.
m.s: Determines the starting state of `Class.Humanoid.UseJumpPower` for `Class.Player.Character`.

kid.simple: Picks which jump setting characters start with: true uses CharacterJumpPower, false uses CharacterJumpHeight. Default true.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CharacterUseJumpPower = false

m.d:
This property determines the starting value of Humanoid.WalkSpeed for a player's Player.Character with a default of 16.

Since this property is only relevant for characters being spawned in the future, changing it will not change any existing player characters. Changes to this property will only take effect when a player respawns.
m.s: Determines the starting value of `Class.Humanoid.WalkSpeed` for `Class.Player.Character`.

kid.simple: Starting walk speed in studs per second (default 16). Takes effect on respawn.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.CharacterWalkSpeed = 20

m.d: When enabled, the character uses the classic death behavior (joints break apart and parts scatter). When disabled, characters spawn with Humanoid.BreakJointsOnDeath = false, and will ragdoll when they die.
m.s: Controls whether the character uses the classic death behavior when the Humanoid's health reaches zero.

kid.simple: If true, characters break apart when they die (the classic Roblox 'oof'). If false, they ragdoll (go floppy) instead.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.ClassicDeath = false

m.d: This property is only visible when Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem is enabled. When set to true (default), the PlayerModule injection point occurs at StarterPlayer. When set to false, the default camera and control scripts will not be added to the place.
m.s: Controls how the default player module and related scripts are handled.

kid.simple: Internal setting (scripts can't use it). Controls whether Roblox adds its default camera and control scripts.

m.d:
Defines how the default camera scripts handle objects between the camera and the camera subject. Applies to all players as they join the experience and can't be changed for individual players.

The default value is Zoom (0). See DevCameraOcclusionMode for a list of available modes.
m.s: Sets how the default camera handles objects between the camera and the player.

kid.simple: What the camera does when a wall blocks the view of the character: Zoom (moves closer, the default) or Invisicam (makes the wall see-through). Applies to everyone.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.DevCameraOcclusionMode = Enum.DevCameraOcclusionMode.Invisicam

m.d:
This property lets you overwrite the player's camera mode on a computer.

If set to UserChoice, the player's camera movement mode will be determined by whatever they set in the experience's settings. Otherwise, the mode will be set based on this property.

This property does not affect players who are not on a computer.
m.s: Lets you overwrite the player's camera mode on a computer.

kid.simple: Forces a camera style for computer players. UserChoice lets each player pick in their settings.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.DevComputerCameraMovementMode = Enum.DevComputerCameraMovementMode.Classic

m.d:
This property lets you overwrite the player's movement mode on a computer.

If set to UserChoice, the player's movement mode will be determined by whatever they set in the experience's settings. Otherwise, the mode will be set based on this property.

This property does not affect players who are not on a computer.
m.s: Lets you overwrite the player's movement mode on a computer.

kid.simple: Forces a movement style for computer players, like KeyboardMouse or ClickToMove. UserChoice lets each player pick.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.DevComputerMovementMode = Enum.DevComputerMovementMode.KeyboardMouse

m.d:
This property lets you overwrite the player's camera mode on a touch-enabled device.

If set to UserChoice, the player's camera movement mode will be determined by whatever they set in the experience's settings. Otherwise, the mode will be set based on this property.

This property does not affect players who are not on a touch-enabled device.
m.s: Lets you overwrite the player's camera mode on a touch-enabled device.

kid.simple: Forces a camera style for touch-screen players. UserChoice lets each player pick.

m.d:
Lets you overwrite the player's movement mode on a touch-enabled device.

If set to UserChoice, the player's movement mode will be determined by whatever they set in the experience's settings. Otherwise, the mode will be set based on this property.

This property does not affect players who are not on a touch-enabled device.
m.s: Lets you overwrite the player's movement mode on a touch-enabled device.

kid.simple: Forces a movement control for touch-screen players, like Thumbstick or DPad. UserChoice lets each player pick.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.DevTouchMovementMode = Enum.DevTouchMovementMode.Thumbstick

m.d: Sets the use of dynamic heads. When true, enables the use of avatar heads with facial animation data.
m.s: Sets the use of dynamic heads. When true, enables the use of avatar heads with facial animation data.

kid.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). Allows avatar heads that can move their faces (blink, smile).

m.d:
This property determines if a player can toggle mouse lock by default.

Mouselock will lock the player's cursor to the center of the screen. Moving the mouse will rotate the Camera and Player will move relative to the current rotation of the camera.

This property sets the value of Player.DevEnableMouseLock.

Note that shift-lock related APIs are in the process of being deprecated, so it's recommended to use UserInputService.MouseBehavior instead to lock the mouse.
m.s: Determines if a player can toggle mouse lock by default.

kid.simple: Whether players can turn on shift lock (mouse locked in the middle, camera turns with the mouse). Copied to Player.DevEnableMouseLock.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.EnableMouseLockOption = false

m.d:
This property sets the distance in studs at which this player will see other Humanoid health bars. If set to 0, the health bars will not be displayed. This property is set to 100 studs by default.

To change the display distance for a player once they join the game, you can set the Player.HealthDisplayDistance property.

If a Humanoid health bar is visible, you can set the display type using Humanoid.DisplayDistanceType.
m.s: Sets the distance at which this player will see other `Class.Humanoid` health bars. If set to 0, the health bars will not be displayed.

kid.simple: Starting distance (in studs) at which players see other characters' health bars. Default 100. 0 hides them.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.HealthDisplayDistance = 0

m.d:
This property sets whether or not the appearance of a player's character should be loaded.

Setting this to false results in the player having no clothes (including hats), body colors, body packages or anything else related to the appearance of the player's avatar. By default, this property is set to true.

Setting this to true results in the player loading the appearance corresponding to the player's Player.CharacterAppearanceId.

If Player:LoadCharacterWithHumanoidDescriptionAsync() is used, it can be advantageous to set StarterPlayer.LoadCharacterAppearance to false as the player's avatar is not required as all asset IDs to equip on the character will come from the passed in HumanoidDescription.
m.s: Whether or not the appearance of a player's character should be loaded.

kid.simple: If true (default), players spawn wearing their own avatar. If false, they spawn plain: no clothes, hats or body colors. Handy if you dress everyone yourself with a HumanoidDescription.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.LoadCharacterAppearance = false

m.d:
Indicates whether characters spawning into an experience will have layered clothing accessories equipped on them (Although Workspace.MeshPartHeadsAndAccessories also need to be enabled in the Workspace).

This property also gates the WrapLayer.AutoSkin feature. When set to Disabled, the automatic skinning transfer pipeline for WrapLayers does not run, and WrapLayer.AutoSkin has no effect. For more information, see Automatic Skinning Transfer.
m.s: Indicates whether characters spawning into an experience will have layered clothing accessories equipped on them.

kid.simple: A Studio setting (scripts can't change it). Whether spawning characters wear their layered 3D clothing like jackets.

m.d: Determines which character controller implementation drives the player's character movement. Accepts a value from CharacterControlMode: Default, Legacy, NoCharacterController, or LuaCharacterController.
m.s: Sets the character controller mode used by the player's character.

kid.simple: Picks which system moves player characters: Default, Legacy, LuaCharacterController, or NoCharacterController. Most games leave it on Default.

m.d:
Sets the distance at which this player will see other Humanoid names. If set to 0, names are hidden. This property is set to 100 studs by default.

To change the display distance for a player once they join the game, you can set the Player.NameDisplayDistance property.

If a Humanoid name is visible, you can set the display type using Humanoid.DisplayDistanceType.
m.s: Sets the distance at which this player will see other `Class.Humanoid` names.

kid.simple: Starting distance (in studs) at which players see other characters' names. Default 100. 0 hides names.
kid.example: StarterPlayer.NameDisplayDistance = 40

m.d:
This property determines if user-owned emotes are loaded when loading avatars. Setting this property to false disables loading. Developers can set the property in Studio directly.

When emote loading is disabled, the emotes UI will still work as long as developers choose to use the emotes feature by adding emotes within their game.

See also Avatar Emotes, an article detailing how to control, customize, and play avatar emotes.
m.s: Determines if user-owned emotes are loaded when loading avatars.

kid.simple: If true, players' own emotes are loaded with their avatar. Set it in Studio. If false, only emotes your game adds are available.

StarterPlayer holds the starting settings for every player and their character, like walk speed, jump power, camera zoom limits, and whether to use their own avatar. When someone joins, these values are copied onto their Player and character. It also holds two script folders: StarterPlayerScripts and StarterCharacterScripts.
kid.analogy: StarterPlayer is like the 'new player starter kit' settings page. Whatever you set here is what every new player starts with. Players who are already in the game don't change when you edit it.
whenToUse: Change everyone's default walk speed, jump power, or slope limit.
Limit how far the camera can zoom, or force first person.
Choose whether players look like their own avatar (LoadCharacterAppearance).
Put LocalScripts that run once per player in StarterPlayerScripts.
Put scripts that go inside the character every spawn in StarterCharacterScripts.
kid.where: A service in the Explorer. Usually set its properties in Studio's Properties window. From code: `game:GetService("StarterPlayer")`. Its child folders: StarterPlayerScripts (copied once into each Player's PlayerScripts when they join) and StarterCharacterScripts (copied into the Character every time it spawns). You can also add a Humanoid named StarterHumanoid or a Model named StarterCharacter to replace the default ones.

terms.default: The value something starts with if nobody changes it.
terms.StarterPlayerScripts: A folder in StarterPlayer. Its LocalScripts are copied once into each player's PlayerScripts when they join, and keep running across deaths. Good for input, camera, and UI managers.
terms.StarterCharacterScripts: A folder in StarterPlayer. Its scripts are copied into the character every time it spawns, so they restart each life. Good for things tied to the body, like a sprint script.
terms.PlayerScripts: A folder inside each Player that holds copies of StarterPlayerScripts. Only that player's device can see it.
terms.StarterCharacter: A Model you name StarterCharacter and put in StarterPlayer. Every player will spawn as a copy of it instead of their avatar.
terms.StarterHumanoid: A Humanoid you name StarterHumanoid and put in StarterPlayer. Its settings are used for every character's Humanoid.
terms.stud: Roblox's distance unit. A default character is about 5 studs tall.
terms.respawn: Getting a new character after dying.
terms.mouse lock: Also called shift lock. Locks the mouse in the middle of the screen so the camera turns as you move the mouse.

examples.title: Set defaults for every player (by script)
examples.code:
local StarterPlayer = game:GetService("StarterPlayer")

-- Every character that spawns from now on gets these
StarterPlayer.CharacterWalkSpeed = 24      -- default is 16
StarterPlayer.CharacterUseJumpPower = true
StarterPlayer.CharacterJumpPower = 70       -- default is 50

-- Camera limits for players who join from now on
StarterPlayer.CameraMaxZoomDistance = 30
StarterPlayer.CameraMinZoomDistance = 5
explain: Character* settings are copied into each character's Humanoid when it spawns. Characters already in the world keep their old values until they respawn.
Camera* settings are copied onto the Player when they join.
Usually you just type these into the Properties window in Studio instead of using a script.

examples.title: Where to put player scripts
examples.code:
-- Because this is in StarterCharacterScripts, a fresh copy is placed
-- INSIDE the character every time it spawns. script.Parent is the character.
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

-- Hold Left Shift to sprint
UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, typing)
    if not typing and input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift then
        humanoid.WalkSpeed = 28
    end
end)
UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(input)
    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift then
        humanoid.WalkSpeed = 16
    end
end)
explain: StarterCharacterScripts -> copied into the Character on every spawn. The script restarts each life, and script.Parent is the new character, so you always have the right Humanoid.
StarterPlayerScripts -> copied once into the Player's PlayerScripts when they join. Those scripts keep running even when the character dies.
typing is true when the player is typing in a text box (like chat), so we ignore those key presses.

gotchas: Changing StarterPlayer while the game runs only affects characters spawned (or players joining) afterward.
CharacterJumpPower only matters when CharacterUseJumpPower is true; CharacterJumpHeight only when it's false.
Scripts in StarterPlayerScripts don't restart on death; scripts in StarterCharacterScripts do.
Server Scripts placed in StarterPlayerScripts won't run, because the server can't see PlayerScripts.

class/StarterPlayerScripts.d:
StarterPlayerScripts is a container object located within the StarterPlayer service. It can contain LocalScripts and other objects to be copied to the PlayerScripts container once when a Player joins the game. For example, if you want to create special effects on the client when certain conditions are met, you can place a LocalScript within this container to do that.

When an experience is run, this object will also house the default multi-platform Roblox control scripts for the camera and character. If LocalScripts named CameraScript or ControlScript are placed within this container, they will replace the Roblox defaults for those scripts respectively. If desired, you can add empty LocalScripts for each of these to disable them altogether; this is useful for experiences that do not follow the typical control paradigms of a Roblox experience.
class/StarterPlayerScripts.s: A container for objects to be copied to a Player's PlayerScripts when they join a game.

class/Stats.d:
Stats is a service that provides real-time performance information about the current running game instance. Its primary purpose is to provide an end point to measure where resources are being consumed, as well as how much memory is being consumed overall.

The service also stores a tree of StatsItem objects which can have their values read by plugins.

m.d: This property describes how many parts are currently in contact with each other, such that one of the two parts are being physically simulated, and thus can be recognized by the BasePart:GetTouchingParts() method.
m.s: A measurement of how many parts are currently in contact with one another.

m.d: In a networked game, this property describes roughly how many kilobytes of data are being received by the current instance, per second. If from the server's perspective, this represents the total amount of data being received from the clients connected to the server. If from a client's perspective, this represents the total amount of data being received from the server.
m.s: In a networked game, this describes roughly how many kilobytes of data are being received by the current instance, per second.

m.d: In a networked game, this property describes roughly how many kilobytes of data are being sent by the current instance, per second. If from the server's perspective, this represents the total amount of data being sent to the clients connected to the server. If from a client's perspective, this represents the total amount of data being sent to the server.
m.s: In a networked game, this describes roughly how many kilobytes of data are being sent by the current instance, per second.

m.d: This property is only available in client scripts and is a measurement of how long it took to render the most-recent frame in seconds. Divide 1 by this value to calculate an FPS value for the frame time. High frame times are indicative of performance problems on the device. Consider using the MicroProfiler to troubleshoot.
m.s: A measurement of how long it takes for the engine to process all tasks required to render a frame.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the total amount of time it takes for the server to update its task scheduler jobs in seconds. If this value is high, examine server compute.
m.s: A measurement of the total amount of time it takes for the server to update its task scheduler jobs in seconds.

m.d: The HeartbeatTimeMs property is a measurement of the total amount of time it takes long it takes for Roblox to update all of its task scheduler jobs, in milliseconds. If this value is high, then it means one of the tasks are hogging up a lot of resources.
m.s: A measurement of the total amount of time it takes long it takes for Roblox to update all of its task scheduler jobs, in milliseconds.
m.dep: Use Stats.HeartbeatTime instead.

m.d: InstanceCount is a read-only measurement of how many Instance are currently in memory. This includes the DataModel, its descendants, as well as any object created with Instance.new() which is still present in memory.
m.s: A measurement of how many `Class.Instance` are currently in memory.

m.d: If MemoryTrackingEnabled returns false, any API that returns category-based memory usage such as Stats:GetMemoryUsageMbForTag() or Stats:GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories() will return 0 and emit a warning. Therefore, usage of category-based memory usage API should be conditional on MemoryTrackingEnabled returning true. The value of MemoryTrackingEnabled will not change from one experience to the next; it will only potentially change after restarting the Roblox client application.
m.s: An indication of whether memory tracking is enabled. This is guaranteed to be unchanged until the next time the Client is started.

m.d: A measurement of how many physically simulated components are currently moving in the game world.
m.s: A measurement of how many physically simulated components are currently moving in the game world.

m.d: PhysicsReceiveKbps is a measurement of roughly how many kilobytes of physics data are being received by the current instance, per second.If from the server's perspective, this represents the total amount of physics data being received from the clients connected to the server.If from a client's perspective, this represents the total amount of physics data being received from the server.
m.s: In a networked game, this describes roughly how many kilobytes of physics data are being received by the current instance, per second.

m.d: PhysicsSendKbps describes roughly how many kilobytes of physics data are being sent by the current instance, per second. If from the server's perspective, this represents the total amount of physics data being sent to the clients connected to the server. If from a client's perspective, this represents the total amount of physics data being sent to the server.
m.s: In a networked game, this describes roughly how many kilobytes of physics data are being sent by the current instance, per second.

m.d: This property is a measurement of how long it takes for the physics engine to update its current state. If this value is high, it means the game instance is under stress from the physics simulations taking place.
m.s: A measurement of how long it takes for the physics engine to update its current state.

m.d: A measurement of how long it takes for the physics engine to update its current state, in milliseconds. If this value is high, then it means the game instance is under stress from the physics simulations taking place.
m.s: A measurement of how long it takes for the physics engine to update its current state, in milliseconds. If this value is high, then it means the game instance is under stress from the physics simulations taking place.
m.dep: Use Stats.PhysicsStepTime instead.

m.d: A measurement of how many physically simulated components currently exist in the game world.
m.s: A measurement of how many physically simulated components currently exist in the game world.

m.d: This property is a measurement of how long it takes for the CPU to process all of its rendering tasks for a frame.
m.s: A measurement of how long it takes for the CPU to process all of its rendering tasks for a frame.

m.d: This property is a measurement of how long it takes for the GPU to process all of its tasks required to render a frame.
m.s: A measurement of how long it takes for the GPU to process all of its tasks required to render a frame.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of draw calls made by the game's current scene. A draw call is a single rendering operation, such as drawing a mesh. A high draw call count could mean a scene is too complex or unoptimized, which can lead to performance issues.
m.s: A measurement of the number of draw calls made by the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of triangles rendered by the game's current scene. A count of triangles rendered is useful when trying to estimate the complexity and performance of a scene.
m.s: A measurement of the number of triangles rendered by the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of draw calls being made for shadows by the game's current scene. A high count means more shadows are being created by the amount of rendered objects in a scene.
m.s: A measurement of the number of draw calls being made for shadows by the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of triangles rendered as shadows in the game's current scene. A high count means there are a lot of triangles used to cast shadows, which can hinder performance.
m.s: A measurement of the number of triangles rendered as shadows in the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of 2D draw calls made for UI elements in the game's current scene. A high count can mean there are a lot of 2D UI elements being used.
m.s: A measurement of the number of 2D draw calls made for UI elements in the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of triangles that are being rendered for 2D UI elements in the game's current scene. A high count can mean there are many or complex 2D UI elements used, which can contribute to performance loss in regards to rendering.
m.s: A measurement of the number of triangles that are being rendered for 2D UI elements in the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of 3D draw calls made for UI elements in the game's current scene. A high count could indicate a high amount of 3D objects being used within UI, potentially hurting performance; however, it is very unlikely you would see a significant count since UI elements are typically 2D.
m.s: A measurement of the number of 3D draw calls made for UI elements in the game's current scene.

m.d: This property is a measurement of the number of triangles being rendered for 3D UI elements in the game's current scene; however, it is very unlikely you would see a significant count since UI elements are typically 2D.
m.s: A measurement of the number of triangles being rendered for 3D UI elements in the game's current scene.

m.d: Requires the InternalTest security capability; not callable from ordinary scripts. Returns the current quality level selected by the engine's dynamic performance-control system, expressed as a score normalized between 0 (the lowest-quality configuration) and 100 (the highest). The score reflects how the system is currently balancing visual quality against resource usage such as memory and frame time.
m.s: Internal-only. Returns the engine's current dynamic-quality level as a score normalized from `0` to `100`.

r.s: The current dynamic-quality level, normalized from 0 (lowest quality) to 100 (highest quality).

m.d: Requires the InternalTest security capability; not callable from ordinary scripts. Returns an array of strings containing the name of every memory category the engine tracks, in category-index order. The entries correspond one-to-one with the measurements returned by Stats:GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories(), so the two arrays can be read together to label each per-category memory value.
m.s: Internal-only. Returns an array of the names of every developer memory category the engine tracks.

r.s: An array of strings, one per tracked memory category, ordered to match the values returned by Stats:GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories().

m.d: Returns the number of megabytes that are being consumed by all available categories. If MemoryTrackingEnabled is false, calling GetMemoryUsageMbAllCategories() will return an empty array and emit a warning to the console.
m.s: Returns the number of megabytes that are being consumed by all available categories, or an empty array if `Class.Stats.MemoryTrackingEnabled|MemoryTrackingEnabled` is `false`.

r.s: An array of numbers in which each entry is the memory, in megabytes, consumed by one memory category, ordered to match the categories returned by Stats:GetMemoryCategoryNames(). Returns an empty array if MemoryTrackingEnabled is false.

m.d: Returns the number of megabytes that are being consumed in the specified DeveloperMemoryTag category. If MemoryTrackingEnabled is false, calling GetMemoryUsageMbForTag() will return 0 and emit a warning to the console.
m.s: Returns the number of megabytes that are being consumed in the specified `Enum.DeveloperMemoryTag` category, or `0` if `Class.Stats.MemoryTrackingEnabled|MemoryTrackingEnabled` is `false`.

p.s: The DeveloperMemoryTag memory category to measure.

r.s: The memory, in megabytes, consumed by the given DeveloperMemoryTag category, or 0 if MemoryTrackingEnabled is false.

m.d:
Returns the total amount of memory being consumed by the current game session, in megabytes.

This method gets memory usage from the operating system, which may exclude memory that has been paged out to disk. As such, the return value tends to differ significantly from the sum of usage for all DeveloperMemoryTags. The return value should be very similar to memory usage for Roblox in the Windows Task Manager or macOS Activity Monitor.

m.d: Requires the InternalTest security capability; not callable from ordinary scripts. Reverts the artificial memory budget applied by Stats:SetHarmonyMemoryTarget(), restoring the memory-override enable state and limit that were captured before the first call to SetHarmonyMemoryTarget(). After this call, the performance-control system resumes using the device's real available memory when making dynamic-quality decisions.
m.s: Internal-only. Restores the performance-control system's memory budget to the values in effect before `Class.Stats:SetHarmonyMemoryTarget()` was called.

m.d: Requires the InternalTest security capability; not callable from ordinary scripts. Forces the engine's dynamic performance-control system to operate against an artificial memory budget of targetMB megabytes instead of the device's real available memory, making it behave as though only that much memory is available. This lets you test how dynamic quality and memory reclamation respond under a chosen level of memory pressure. The first call records the pre-override settings so that a later call to Stats:ResetHarmonyMemoryTarget() can restore them.
m.s: Internal-only. Overrides the performance-control system's memory budget with a target value, in megabytes, for testing.

p.s: The memory budget to impose on the performance-control system, in megabytes.

class/Status.dep:
Status is an unfinished object designed to store custom Humanoid statuses. It has been deprecated and should not be used by developers in new work.

Developers looking to implement custom Humanoid statuses should use Character Physics Controllers, as they are written in Luau and are easily extendable.

class/StopWatchReporter.d:
Not available to creator scripts. StopWatchReporter is used by the Roblox app to measure the duration of logic flows. Each measurement is classified by device platform and country code.

The service groups timing measurements into named reports. Starting a task begins timing a named task within a report and returns an integer task ID; finishing a task stops that task's timer; and sending a report finalizes it, submitting the elapsed time of each finished task and preventing any further tasks from being added to that report.

Timing is only collected on the Android and iOS clients; on other platforms these methods do nothing and starting a task returns -1.
class/StopWatchReporter.s: A service that times named tasks and reports their durations, classified by device platform and country code. Not available to creator scripts.

class/StringValue.d:
Stores a single Luau string. The length of the string can't be more than 200,000 characters; anything longer causes a String too long error.

If the string is too long to be displayed in the Value field within the Properties window, it shows partial string contents and an ellipsis (...).

Like all ValueBase objects, this single value is stored in the Value property. The Changed event fires with the new value being stored in the object, instead of a string representing the property being changed.

class/StudioCaptureService.d: StudioCaptureService is a Studio-only service that lets plugins capture screenshots of the active place's 3D viewport. Use RequestScreenshotPermissionAsync() to obtain the user's permission, CanCaptureScreenshot() to check whether a capture is currently possible, and CaptureScreenshot() to request an image of the current view. All members require plugin security and are only available within Studio.
class/StudioCaptureService.s: A Studio-only service that lets plugins capture screenshots of the active place's 3D viewport.

m.d: Returns false when there is a known reason a screenshot cannot be captured — for example, when this is not the active DataModel or the plugin does not have permission — and true otherwise. A return value of true does not guarantee that CaptureScreenshot() will succeed, because conditions can change between the two calls.
m.s: Returns whether a screenshot can currently be captured.

r.s: A boolean that is false when a screenshot is known to be uncapturable, or true otherwise.

m.d:
Captures a screenshot of the active DataModel according to screenshotOptions and returns a StudioScreenshotCapture in the requested format. If an image of the requested size cannot be captured at the requested position, the capture fails rather than clipping the image.

The screenshotOptions dictionary accepts the following keys:

  • Position — a Vector2 top-left offset of the captured region. Must be non-negative and defaults to (0, 0).
  • CaptureSize — a Vector2 size of the region to capture. Both components must be positive.
  • OutputSize — a Vector2 size of the returned image. Both components must be positive; when it differs from CaptureSize, ResampleMode must also be provided.
  • ResampleMode — the resampling filter used when OutputSize differs from CaptureSize.
  • Format — an StudioCaptureScreenshotFormat for the returned buffer. Defaults to StudioCaptureScreenshotFormat.RGBA8.
  • UICaptureMode — an UICaptureMode controlling whether UI is included in the capture. Defaults to UICaptureMode.All.

The returned StudioScreenshotCapture is populated asynchronously: its image buffer becomes available only after the capture and encoding complete, and any errors are reported on the capture object.
m.s: Captures a screenshot of the active place according to the provided options.

p.s: A dictionary of options controlling the capture, such as Position, CaptureSize, OutputSize, ResampleMode, Format, and UICaptureMode.

r.s: A StudioScreenshotCapture that holds the requested image in the requested format.

m.d: This yielding function asks the user to grant the plugin permission to capture screenshots from their Studio 3D view, returning true if permission is granted and false otherwise. It can return immediately without prompting when the plugin's permission is already known from an earlier session, and it returns false without prompting when the global screenshot setting is disabled.
m.s: Requests the user's permission for the plugin to capture screenshots from the Studio 3D view.

r.s: A boolean that is true if the user granted permission and false otherwise.

class/StudioDeviceSimulatorService.d:
Provides programmatic control over Studio's Device Simulator. Use this service to switch between device presets, override resolution and pixel density, control orientation and scaling, and manage custom device profiles from a plugin or from an external tool connected through the MCP server.

All methods are asynchronous and yield the calling coroutine. The service is available in Edit mode and Play Client. Methods that modify the active simulation state are blocked in PlayServer mode.

Limitations
  • All methods are asynchronous and yield the calling coroutine.
  • Methods that modify the active simulation state (SetDeviceAsync, StopSimulationAsync, SetOrientationAsync, SetResolutionAsync, SetPixelDensityAsync, SetScalingModeAsync) error in PlayServer mode. They work in Edit mode and Play Client.
  • UpdateDeviceAsync and RemoveDeviceAsync error when called on built-in presets.
  • Resolution, DPI, and scaling mode methods require an active device and error when GetDeviceAsync() returns "default".
  • Resolution and DPI overrides are session-level. They are not persisted and are cleared on SetDeviceAsync.
  • Built-in presets are immutable.
class/StudioDeviceSimulatorService.s: Service allowing you to control Studio's Device Simulator.

m.d:
Creates a custom device and returns its newly assigned ID. Custom devices are persisted to disk and appear in the Device Simulator UI.

Errors if any required field is missing or out of range.
m.s: Creates a custom device preset and returns its ID.

p.s: A dictionary describing the new device. Required fields: Name (string, 1-200 characters, cannot be "default"), Width (int, 1-7680 pixels), Height (int, 1-4320 pixels), PixelDensity (int, 72-10000 DPI). Optional fields: DeviceForm (DeviceForm, default Phone), ResolutionScale (float, default 1.0, max 10.0), PortraitKeyboardHeight (int, default 0), LandscapeKeyboardHeight (int, default 0).

r.s: string

m.d: Returns the ID of the currently active device, or "default" if no device is active.
m.s: Returns the ID of the currently active device, or `"default"` if none is active.

r.s: string

m.d:
Returns a DeviceConfiguration for the specified device without activating it. Useful for inspecting presets before choosing one to switch to.

The returned dictionary contains the following fields:

Field Type Create/Update Description
DeviceId string Read-only Unique identifier assigned by the service.
Name string Required Display name. 1 to 200 characters. Cannot be "default".
Width number Required Screen width in pixels. Range: 1 to 7680.
Height number Required Screen height in pixels. Range: 1 to 4320.
PixelDensity number Required Pixel density in DPI. Range: 72 to 10000.
DeviceForm Enum.DeviceForm Optional (default: Phone) One of Phone, Tablet, Desktop, Console, VR.
IsCustom boolean Read-only true if the device was user-created.
ResolutionScale number Optional (default: 1.0) Resolution scaling factor. Must be greater than 0, max 10.0.
PortraitKeyboardHeight number Optional (default: 0) Virtual keyboard height in portrait mode.
LandscapeKeyboardHeight number Optional (default: 0) Virtual keyboard height in landscape mode.
m.s: Returns the configuration dictionary for the specified device.

p.s: The unique identifier of the device to query. Must be a valid ID from GetDeviceListAsync(); cannot be "default".

r.s: A dictionary containing the device configuration and passed to CreateDeviceAsync and UpdateDeviceAsync.

m.d: Returns an array of device IDs for all available presets, including built-in and custom devices.
m.s: Returns an array of all available device IDs.

r.s: An array of device IDs.

m.d: Returns the current simulated orientation.
m.s: Returns the current simulated screen orientation.

r.s: ScreenOrientation

m.d: Returns the current simulated pixel density.
m.s: Returns the current simulated pixel density in DPI.

r.s: number

m.d: Returns the current simulated resolution.
m.s: Returns the current simulated viewport resolution.

r.s: Vector2

Returns the current DeviceSimulatorScalingMode for how the simulated resolution maps to the Studio viewport. See SetScalingModeAsync() for the available modes.

Requires an active device; errors when GetDeviceAsync() returns "default".
m.s: Returns how the simulated resolution currently maps to the Studio viewport.

Removes a custom device.
